skill.name: copy-editing
skill.description: When the user wants to edit, review, or improve existing marketing copy, or refresh outdated content. Also use when the user mentions 'edit this copy,' 'review my copy,' 'copy feedback,' 'proofread,' 'polish this,' 'make this better,' 'copy sweep,' 'tighten this up,' 'this reads awkwardly,' 'clean up this text,' 'too wordy,' 'sharpen the messaging,' 'refresh this content,' 'update this page,' 'this content is outdated,' or 'content audit.' Use this when the user already has copy and wants it improved or refreshed rather than rewritten from scratch. For writing new copy, see copywriting.
skill.summary: Improve existing marketing copy through focused reviews of clarity, tone, benefits, proof, specificity, emotion, and conversion risk.
skill.author: coreyhaines31

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives caused by ordinary prose or Markdown filename formatting. No command execution, system reconnaissance, prompt injection, or other semantic security issue was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: The line is a plain-English table entry that replaces "aforesaid" with simpler words. It contains no system reconnaissance instruction or executable command.
The line is a vocabulary table entry that defines "outstanding" as "unpaid." It does not request or perform system reconnaissance.
The backticks are Markdown delimiters around local filenames, not Ruby or shell execution syntax. The instruction only asks the agent to read existing marketing context.

content.value_statement: Weak or outdated marketing copy can hide value and reduce reader confidence. This skill improves clarity, proof, specificity, tone, and calls to action through focused editing passes.
actual_capabilities: Reviews existing marketing copy through seven focused editing passes.
Identifies unclear language, inconsistent tone, vague claims, and weak calls to action.
Connects product features to specific reader benefits and desired outcomes.
Flags unsupported claims and recommends proof or more careful wording.
Performs quick word, sentence, and paragraph checks for shorter reviews.
Audits published content for outdated facts, links, examples, voice, and search intent.
limitations: This skill improves existing copy and does not create complete marketing pages from scratch.
It cannot confirm factual claims without reliable sources or current product information.
Expert panel scores represent simulated perspectives, not reviews from independent people.
Its recommendations do not replace legal, regulatory, or brand approval.

use_cases.title: Improve a landing page
use_cases.description: Review benefits, proof, specificity, and calls to action before a campaign launches.

use_cases.title: Refresh published content
use_cases.description: Find stale data, outdated product details, weak links, and changes in search intent.

use_cases.title: Tighten product messaging
use_cases.description: Remove filler and sharpen an existing product description while preserving its core message.

prompt_templates.title: Quick copy edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Tighten this marketing copy without changing its core message: [paste copy]. Identify the main issues, then provide a concise revision.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a fast review of a short section.

prompt_templates.title: Run the seven sweeps
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this copy with all seven sweeps: [paste copy]. The audience is [audience], and the desired action is [action]. Explain each recommended edit.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a complete review of a page or campaign.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh existing content
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this published content for stale facts, links, examples, brand voice, proof, and search intent: [paste content]. Separate updates from full rewrite recommendations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when an existing page is outdated or losing traffic.

prompt_templates.title: Score high-stakes copy
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this copy through relevant expert perspectives: [paste copy]. Score each perspective, explain the weakest areas, revise them, and score the revision again.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for launch, pricing, sales, or other high-stakes copy.

output_examples.input: Ready to take your business to the next level? Click here to learn more about how we can help.
output_examples.output: The opening is generic, and the action is unclear. Revision: See how CloudSync shortens project handoffs and keeps every owner informed.

output_examples.input: Review a product page with old statistics, outdated feature names, and declining search traffic.
output: Replace old statistics with sourced, current figures.
Update feature names and remove deprecated capabilities.
Compare the page structure with current search intent.
Preserve useful sections and rewrite only sections with outdated positioning.

best_practices: Provide the target audience, copy goal, desired action, and current brand guidance.
Supply reliable evidence for statistics, testimonials, guarantees, and product claims.
Choose a quick pass for small edits and the full framework for important copy.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to create an entire page without an existing draft.
Do not invent proof, customer results, statistics, guarantees, or product details.
Do not change the core message without explaining the change and obtaining approval.

faq.question: What types of copy can this skill review?
faq.answer: It can review landing pages, pricing pages, emails, product descriptions, sales pages, advertisements, and published content.

faq.question: Can it write copy from scratch?
faq.answer: No. It is designed to improve an existing draft while preserving the original message.

faq.question: What are the seven editing sweeps?
faq.answer: They cover clarity, voice and tone, reader value, proof, specificity, emotion, and barriers to action.

faq.question: Can it preserve our brand voice?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide current brand guidance and customer language so the edits can follow them.

faq.question: Will it verify every claim?
faq.answer: It flags claims that need support, but users must provide reliable sources and current product facts.

faq.question: When should I request a content refresh?
faq.answer: Use a refresh when facts, examples, links, features, positioning, brand voice, or search intent have changed.
